title: Drop repeated words, keep first-seen order

blocks.text: The page warns that a `HashSet` does **not** keep insertion order: it rejects duplicates, but it iterates in whatever order its buckets give. A set compares elements with `equals` and `hashCode`, never with `==`.

Write `Dedupe.distinct(List<String> words)`. It returns a **new** list holding each distinct word once, in the order the words were **first seen**. Two words are the same word when their text is equal, even if they are different `String` objects. The input list is not changed.

cases.says: Each word appears once in the answer, in the order it was first seen.
Words come back in the order they arrived, even when a hash set would iterate them in another order.
A repeated word stays at the place it was first seen; a later repeat does not move it.
Two distinct String objects with the same text are the same word.
"Aa" and "BB" share a hash code but are two words, and so are "Hello" and "hello": equality is the text, exactly.
Each call returns a new list of its own, even when nothing repeats, and a later call does not change an earlier answer.

concepts: A HashSet does not keep insertion order; an ordered set such as LinkedHashSet keeps the order elements were first added.
A set refuses an element equal to one it already holds, comparing by equals and hashCode rather than by identity.
